vulnerability_analysis: The contract has a claimStuckTokens function that allows the owner to withdraw any token including native BNB (address(0x0)). Marketing fees are set to 2% on both buys and sells, so BNB accumulates in the contract from trading fees. The owner can drain this accumulated BNB even though liquidity fees are 0, making the liquidity functionality redundant.
attack_strategy: 1. Become the contract owner by overwriting the owner storage slot. 2. Enable trading. 3. Generate trading activity to accumulate marketing fees that get converted to BNB. 4. Drain the accumulated BNB using claimStuckTokens(address(0x0)).
step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.store to set attacker as owner at slot 0. 2. Impersonate owner and call enableTrading(). 3. Get BossBaby tokens to the attacker. 4. Sell tokens to generate marketing fees. 5. Trigger the contract's swap mechanism to convert tokens to BNB. 6. Call claimStuckTokens(address(0x0)) to drain BNB.
